## Journal Articles

**Penguin, M., & Albatross, A. (2024).** Waddling Through the Twittersphere: Computational
Analysis of Information Diffusion in Coastal Wildlife Communities.
*Journal of Computer-Mediated Communication*, 29(3), 45–67.
[[DOI]](https://doi.org/10.xxxx/xxxxx) [[PDF]](papers/penguin2024.pdf) [[Code]](https://github.com/MarvinPenguin/twittersphere-study)

<!-- To link a PDF: create a papers/ folder in your repo root, add your PDF there,
     and update the filename above. Remove the [[PDF]] link if you don't have one. -->

<details>
<summary>Abstract</summary>
Using a computational approach to analyse 2.3 million posts, we examine how information
spreads through online communities adjacent to wildlife conservation. Findings suggest
that network topology in penguin-adjacent Twitter communities mirrors flocking patterns
observed in physical colonies — with high clustering, rapid cascade formation, and
susceptibility to coordinated misinformation. Implications for computational communication
science and conservation communication are discussed.

**Keywords:** computational methods, information diffusion, wildlife communication, misinformation
</details>

---

**Rockhopper, E., & Penguin, M. (2023).** Fish or Fake News? Misinformation Sharing Patterns
in Antarctic Online Communities.
*Political Communication*, 40(2), 112–134.
[[DOI]](https://doi.org/10.xxxx/xxxxx) [[Preprint]](https://osf.io/xxxxx)

<details>
<summary>Abstract</summary>
This study examines misinformation sharing in online communities centred around Antarctic
wildlife, using a mixed-methods approach combining automated content analysis with network
mapping. We find that communities sharing misinformation about penguin conservation exhibit
structural properties consistent with echo chambers, including low bridging capital and
high internal density.

**Keywords:** misinformation, echo chambers, political communication, network analysis
</details>
